headline: Separate statements from open questions
subtext: Before replying, recipients and staff can reread the conversation, list what the source has stated, and choose the one fact or document needed next.

The thread shows dated messages about supporting documentation, a reply field, a Send button, and an end-to-end encrypted indicator. The footer says “Sign up at hushline.app!”

social.bluesky: Before replying in a Hush Line conversation, separate what the source has stated from what your team has verified. Note the open questions, then ask for the one fact or document needed next. Make this check part of your shared inbox routine.
social.linkedin:
A sensitive thread can mix what a source has stated, what a recipient has concluded, and what still needs checking.

Before a recipient or staff member replies in Hush Line:

1. Read the full conversation.
2. List what the source has stated. Do not treat it as verified unless your team has checked it.
3. Mark the questions that remain open.
4. Decide which one fact or document would help with the next review.
5. Write a focused request, then remove anything you do not need the source to share.

This keeps the next reply tied to the conversation without asking for extra sensitive details.

Add this five-step check to the reply instructions for everyone who shares your Hush Line inbox.

rationale: The Newman mobile conversation is the only candidate without a prior exact screenshot or content-key match. The playbook uses the thread as support for a fresh review habit: distinguish a source's statements from verified information, identify open questions, and request only what is needed next. This differs from the earlier conversation-thread post about composing and sending a reply from the same screen.
